classification.difficultyReason: Interpret a practical composite shape, calculate the roof height from the given heights, and combine rectangle and triangle areas.

inlines.text: Mark is planning to paint the side of his barn. He has measured it to be 5 m wide,
while the right and left sides are both 2.5 m high.
The barn reaches 3.5 m at its highest point perpendicular to the ground.
How many square metres does he need to paint?

spec.description: Upright barn-side pentagon with a horizontal base, vertical walls and two roof slopes meeting at an apex. The dashed apex-to-base perpendicular has a right-angle marker at its foot.
spec.mathematics: Base 5 m; both wall heights 2.5 m as stated in the prompt; total perpendicular height 3.5 m. The roof triangle height is derived only in the answer.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens remain visible; no calculated lengths, decomposition line or area result appears in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Split the barn side into a rectangle and a triangle. The triangle's perpendicular height is $h$.
$$\begin{align*}
h &= 3.5-2.5 \\
h &= 1\text{ m} \\
A_{\text{rectangle}} &= 5\times2.5 \\
A_{\text{rectangle}} &= 12.5\text{ m}^2 \\
A_{\text{triangle}} &= \frac{5\times1}{2} \\
A_{\text{triangle}} &= 2.5\text{ m}^2 \\
A_{\text{total}} &= 12.5+2.5 \\
A_{\text{total}} &= 15\text{ m}^2
\end{align*}$$
